instantiated_cells.justification: Section 13.66 bars any person from lobbying as a lobbyist unless licensed under § 13.63, and § 13.63(1)(a) provides for obtaining and filing an application for that lobbyist license with the commission.
A lobbyist license expires on December 31 of each even-numbered year, which implies renewal every 2 years (24 months).

The law establishes a lobbyist licensing system (§ 13.63) separate from principal/client registration (§ 13.64) and also requires a distinct written authorization for each principal represented (§ 13.65).

Section 13.621(3) provides that elective state officials, local officials, tribal officials, and legislative employees are not subject to specified lobbying provisions when acting in an official capacity.

Section 13.621(2) exempts agencies that file a statement under § 13.695 and named officials from several lobbying requirements, creating a partial exemption for government agencies rather than a complete exemption from the subchapter.

unscoreable_emissions.reason: The bundled sections provide licensing/authorization requirements but do not state any deadline for a lobbyist to amend/update a lobbyist license/registration record.
The statute requires a lobbyist be licensed and authorized before lobbying (§ 13.66) but does not specify a numeric 'days after first lobbying' registration deadline for the lobbyist.
No bundled provision mentions submitting a photograph as part of a lobbyist license application or registration.
